subject: HealthGrid performance discovery — context window & streaming constraints
messages:
From: marissa_cole
To: Max Liu <max.liu@healthgrid.com>
Cc: ben_carter, laura_bennett
Date: Sun, 7 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HealthGrid performance discovery — context window & streaming constraints

Hi Max / Emily,

Thanks again for the call today — good to dig into the real workload shapes. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we can size a Dedicated pool and define SLO hedges. I attached a short SLO workbook + a small sample of streaming interactions (anonymized) to illustrate token distributions.

Recap of constraints you shared:
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end <= 150 ms for interactive clinician UI; p99 <= 300 ms acceptable with degradations.
- Throughput: steady-state 120–160 requests/sec; peak bursts up to ~400 req/sec during morning syncs.
- Concurrency: ~50 concurrent active sessions (each session may stream partial responses).
- Streaming: partial incremental responses required for UI (low-latency prefix streaming); must support chunked token delivery.
- Context window: typical input (patient + notes + prompts) ~6k tokens average; heavy cases up to 12k tokens. Output: usually <= 1k tokens, but some diagnostic summaries reach ~2k.
- SLA constraints: want failover without user-visible errors; can fall back to shorter-summary model if latency/throughput constraints violate thresholds.

Key performance implications we discussed:
- Long inputs (8k–12k) push KV cache and attention cost; this increases per-token latency and affects batching efficiency.
- Streaming reduces perceived latency but increases RPCs and socket life; needs connection pooling and dynamic batching tuned for smaller partial-chunk sizes.
- For p95 150ms with 12k inputs, we likely need a dedicated, quantized model variant or to enforce an input truncation/embedding + retrieval pre-step to reduce live context.

Suggested option set (we can prototype combinations in a private trial):
1) Dedicated pool w/ quantized Llama-2- style variant for baseline throughput + streaming hooks. Auto-fallback to a lower-cost decoder when burst > 300 req/s.
2) Prefix-KV caching for repeated patient context (saves decoding on long histories). We recommend storing canonical sections (patient demographics, meds) as cached KV entries.
3) Retrieval-augmented flow: run embeddings + retrieval to keep live token window <4–6k for most cases; send long documents as condensed references stored in cache.
4) Streaming config: 64–128 token chunk sizes for first pass; enable adaptive chunking when latency SLO is tight.
5) Canary rollout: start with 25% traffic on dedicated; observe p95/p99 and token-cost per session for 1 week.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm the morning burst window (local times) and whether burst clients are batched by device or by backend job?
- Please share one or two anonymized examples (full payloads) for a 12k-token case so we can run a dry run in our perf lab (we included streaming-pattern-sample.jsonl attached).
- If OK, we’ll provision a 2-week Dedicated trial with KV caching and a quantized model to run a 25% canary. I expect to have a rough cost/latency projection within 5 business days after we ingest samples.

Proposed M.A.P. (mutual action plan):
- Feb 8: HealthGrid sends sample payloads and confirms burst window.
- Feb 9–11: Redwood stands up canary Dedicated pool, configures streaming + KV caching.
- Feb 12–18: Run performance smoke and cost projection; share results.

Attachments: HealthGrid_SLO_workbook_v1.xlsx (SLO workbook, quick knobs), streaming-pattern-sample.jsonl (anonymized traces).

Thanks — looping Ben (SRE-savvy) and Laura (Customer Success) to coordinate the trial setup.

—Marissa

Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HealthGrid performance discovery — context window & streaming constraints

Marissa —

Appreciate the level-set and plan. A few quick clarifications:

1) Morning burst: roughly 07:00–09:30 PT; traffic ramps and is dominated by scheduled imports (backend jobs) rather than interactive users — but we still need interactive fallbacks during bulk runs.
2) Samples: we can share two payloads (one typical ~6k, one heavy ~11.5k) redacted by EOD Feb 8. We’ll also include metadata about whether tokens are dense (lots of text) vs. structured (key: value).
3) Fallbacks: prefer degradation to a short summary model (<= 256 tokens) rather than returning errors. Also want rate-limited retry behavior to avoid queue storms.

One more ask — can the canary include a simulated morning import to exercise bursts? If we provide a job spec, can Redwood kick off a load replay?

Thanks — Max
Max Liu
Head of Product, HealthGrid
max.liu@healthgrid.com
From: ben_carter

Cc: laura_bennett
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HealthGrid performance discovery — context window & streaming constraints

Max / Marissa —

Yes, we can run a replay of the morning import during the canary. A couple of implementation notes from infra:

- Canary topology: we’ll spin up a 6-GPU dedicated pool with auto-burst headroom; quantized runtime (INT8) for the primary model, and a smaller fp16 fallback model for ultra-low-latency short summaries.
- Load replay: send us the job spec and we’ll run it against the canary during a scheduled window (we suggest Feb 10 07:00–08:00 PT). We’ll throttle if grid-level utilization > 70%.
- Streaming best-practices: set initial chunk target to 128 tokens and enable backpressure signals from the client so we don't over-schedule batches.
- Observability: we’ll add per-request tracing IDs and token-level cost breakdowns so you can map sessions to costs.

If that works, Marissa and I will create the canary runbook and invite your infra contact to the run window.

—Ben

Thanks Max — that plan works. Quick confirmations and actions from Redwood to keep momentum:

- HealthGrid will send two sample payloads + morning import job spec by EOD Feb 8 (you indicated today).
- Redwood will provision the canary Dedicated pool and run a controlled morning-import replay on Feb 10 07:00–08:00 PT using your job spec. We’ll watch p95/p99 and token cost and pause if stabilization thresholds hit.
- Canary config: 6-GPU pool, INT8 quantized primary, fp16 short-summary fallback, 128 token streaming chunks, prefix-KV caching enabled.
- Deliverables after run: perf summary (p50/p95/p99), cost per session estimate, recommended knobs (truncate vs retrieval vs split model). Expected delivery: Feb 15.

I’ve uploaded the runbook and a short checklist to the Drive link (see related links). Ben will follow up with an invite for the Feb 10 window and the runbook.

Marissa
